raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
base_link_flags() always linked `-L$CUDA_HOME/lib64 -lcudart`. The pip CUDA wheels (site-packages/nvidia/cu13) ship lib/libcudart.so.13 with no lib64/ and no unversioned libcudart.so, so every JIT module with device code failed to link there with `cannot find -lcudart`.

Look in lib64/ then lib/, and link the versioned soname by name when the unversioned link is missing. Toolkit installs keep exactly the old flags, so existing build keys are unchanged.

## Motivation

Fixes #46418.

When `CUDA_HOME` points at the pip CUDA toolkit (`site-packages/nvidia/cu13`), every JIT module with device code fails to link with `cannot find -lcudart`. `base_link_flags()` always emits `-L$CUDA_HOME/lib64 -lcudart`, but the pip wheels ship only `lib/libcudart.so.13`: no `lib64/` and no unversioned `libcudart.so`. With an FP8 model the server exits at startup, during prefill CUDA-graph capture. #43591 pins this toolkit for JIT use and lists the link layout as out of scope.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/toolchain.py`: `base_link_flags()` gets its libcudart flags from a new `_cudart_link_flags(cuda_root)`. It looks in `lib64/` and then `lib/`. If `libcudart.so` exists it links `-lcudart` as before; otherwise it links the versioned soname by name (`-l:libcudart.so.13`, the shortest match, not `libcudart.so.13.0.96`). With neither present, it falls back to the old flags, so the linker error is unchanged.
- **Toolkit installs keep byte-identical flags**, so existing JIT build keys and caches are unaffected.
- `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_jit_cache.py` gets two cases next to the existing link-flag test, both going through `ninja.generate()` with only `cuda_home` patched:
  - `test_pip_cuda_toolkit_links_the_versioned_cudart`: the regression case. **It fails on current `main`** (`-L…/lib64 -lcudart`) **and passes with the fix.**
  - `test_cuda_toolkit_link_flags_are_unchanged`: guards the toolkit flags. A toolkit's `lib/` must not win over `lib64/`, because the flags are part of the build key.

Not changed: `cuda_stubs_dir()` (`lib64/stubs`, used by a few driver-API modules). The pip wheels ship no `libcuda.so` stub, so that path needs a separate decision. FlashInfer's JIT makes the same `lib64` assumption; that's for its own repo.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: link flags only, with no change to kernels or model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Testing

On an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (SM89), WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04, with this branch's code and the pip CUDA 13.0 toolchain (no system toolkit), `CUDA_HOME=<venv>/nvidia/cu13`:

- `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_jit_cache.py`: 44 passed, via `pytest` and via direct execution as CI runs it. The new regression case fails against the unmodified `toolchain.py` from `main`.
- **End to end**, plain pip layout (no symlinks), `--attention-backend triton --sampling-backend pytorch`, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8`:
  - the server starts;
  - greedy, top-k/top-p and 8 concurrent sampled requests all return 200, and so does `/health_generate`;
  - the freshly built `per_token_group_quant` module's `build.ninja` has `-L<venv>/nvidia/cu13/lib -l:libcudart.so.13`, and its `NEEDED` entry is `libcudart.so.13`, the same soname a toolkit build records.
- Caveat: this machine has glibc 2.43, where CUDA 13.0's `crt/math_functions.h` clashes on `rsqrt` (#45066). For the end-to-end run only, I backported CUDA 13.4's `noexcept(true)` declarations into the venv's header. That's unrelated to this change, and the unit tests don't need it.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

files.patch:
@@ -241,7 +241,24 @@ def base_link_flags(*, with_device: bool) -> List[str]:
         ]
     if is_hip_runtime():
         return flags + [f"-L{rocm_home()}/lib", "-lamdhip64"]
-    return flags + [f"-L{cuda_home()}/lib64", "-lcudart"]
+    return flags + _cudart_link_flags(cuda_home())
+
+
+def _cudart_link_flags(cuda_root: str) -> List[str]:
+    # A toolkit ships lib64/libcudart.so; the pip CUDA wheels (nvidia/cu13) ship only
+    # lib/libcudart.so.<major>, with no unversioned link for a plain -lcudart to find.
+    for lib_dir in (f"{cuda_root}/lib64", f"{cuda_root}/lib"):
+        if os.path.exists(f"{lib_dir}/libcudart.so"):
+            return [f"-L{lib_dir}", "-lcudart"]
+        # Shortest name is the soname (libcudart.so.13, not libcudart.so.13.0.96).
+        versioned = sorted(
+            pathlib.Path(lib_dir).glob("libcudart.so.[0-9]*"),
+            key=lambda path: len(path.name),
+        )
+        if versioned:
+            return [f"-L{lib_dir}", f"-l:{versioned[0].name}"]
+    # Neither layout found: keep the toolkit flags, so the linker names what is missing.
+    return [f"-L{cuda_root}/lib64", "-lcudart"]
 
 
 def compilers() -> Tuple[str, str]:

@@ -14,7 +14,8 @@
 import msgspec
 import pytest
 
-from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import cache, ninja
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.common import is_hip_runtime, is_sail_runtime
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import cache, ninja, toolchain
 from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile.paths import KERNEL_PATH
 from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile.spec import BuildSpec
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
@@ -453,6 +454,44 @@ def test_pure_cpp_module_does_not_link_the_gpu_runtime():
     assert "cudart" in ldflags or "amdhip" in ldflags
 
 
+def _cuda_ldflags(monkeypatch, cuda_root: pathlib.Path) -> str:
+    if is_hip_runtime() or is_sail_runtime():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA runtime link flags only")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(toolchain, "cuda_home", lambda: str(cuda_root))
+    with_device = _spec(cuda_files=("/tmp/a.cu",), cpp_wrappers=(), header_only=False)
+    return next(
+        line
+        for line in ninja.generate(with_device).splitlines()
+        if line.startswith("ldflags = ")
+    )
+
+
+def test_pip_cuda_toolkit_links_the_versioned_cudart(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """A device module must link against the pip CUDA wheels' layout.
+
+    `nvidia/cu13` ships `lib/libcudart.so.13` with no `lib64/` and no unversioned
+    `libcudart.so`, so `-L$CUDA_HOME/lib64 -lcudart` fails with `cannot find -lcudart`.
+    """
+    for name in ("libcudart.so.13", "libcudart.so.13.0.96"):
+        _write(tmp_path / "lib" / name, "")
+    ldflags = _cuda_ldflags(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
+    assert f"-L{tmp_path}/lib -l:libcudart.so.13" in ldflags
+    assert "lib64" not in ldflags
+
+
+def test_cuda_toolkit_link_flags_are_unchanged(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """A toolkit install keeps `-L$CUDA_HOME/lib64 -lcudart` exactly.
+
+    The flags are part of the build key, so any change to them recompiles every
+    cached module; a toolkit's `lib/` must not win over `lib64/`.
+    """
+    _write(tmp_path / "lib64" / "libcudart.so", "")
+    _write(tmp_path / "lib" / "libcudart.so.13", "")
+    ldflags = _cuda_ldflags(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
+    assert f"-L{tmp_path}/lib64 -lcudart" in ldflags
+    assert "-l:" not in ldflags
+
+
 def test_generated_ninja_is_deterministic():
     spec = _spec(cuda_wrappers=(("run", "K::run"),))
     assert ninja.generate(spec) == ninja.generate(spec)
